conventions.convention: Key and transcript alphabets are finite, nonempty, and ordered; quantum registers are nonzero and finite-dimensional. Tensor factors retain the displayed A,B,T,E order.
Public communication is ideally authenticated and visible to Eve. Abort is common to both parties, with no unilateral-abort output blocks.
The ideal output preserves the real abort blocks and accepted transcript-adversary marginal, replacing accepted keys by a uniform shared key independent of both transcript and Eve.

Correctness is unconditional mismatch probability. Secrecy is acceptance probability times conditional trace distance; it is zero at zero acceptance, where conditional accepted states are not defined. Protocol error bounds quantify uniformly over allowed strategies.
State trace distance is half the trace norm.
The key-copy channel copies computational-basis classical blocks and does not clone arbitrary quantum states.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the abort-preserving ideal output, δ_id as its trace distance from the real output, ε_cor as unconditional mismatch probability, and ε_sec as acceptance-weighted conditional secrecy distance, with ε_sec=0 when p_acc=0.
For a finite nonempty ordered set I, a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space H_E, and self-adjoint blocks X_i on H_E, the classical block operator X has ||X||₁=Σ_i||X_i||₁.

For the finite ordered key alphabet and nonzero finite-dimensional transcript and adversary spaces in the Statement, C(X)=Σ_k L_k X L_k† is a quantum channel and sends each classical key block k to the shared-key block (k,k).
For the normalized finite classical A,B,T block state in the Statement, γ=C(ρ_ATE) satisfies D(ρ_ABTE,γ_ABTE)=Pr[K_A≠K_B]=Σ_{a≠b,t}tr(R_E^{a,b,t}).

The real and ideal full outputs are density operators; positive-acceptance normalized states and the displayed marginals and uniform products are density operators. At zero acceptance the ideal output equals the real abort-only state.

For every finite authenticated key-distribution protocol and each fixed allowed adversarial strategy, δ_id≤ε_cor+ε_sec. Uniform bounds on correctness and secrecy give the corresponding uniform sum bound.

Ordered tensor factors and orthonormal product bases.
Nonnegativity and trace-one requirements for all states.
Complete positivity and trace preservation on the full operator space.
Finite ancilla amplification and positivity at ancilla dimension one.
Finite protocol operations and positive-probability conditional states.
Normalization of finite instrument outcome weights.
Density of positive-probability instrument branches.
Complete positivity of the explicit finite key-copy Kraus sum.
Trace norm as the finite sum of singular values.
The half-trace-norm state-distance convention.
Spectral calculation of classical block norms and example distances.
Trace norm equals trace on nonnegative blocks.
Absolute homogeneity and triangle inequality.
Linear-first complex inner-product convention and real eigenvalue calculation.
Adjoint identities for copy operators and self-adjoint blocks.

Finite diagonal-sum trace calculations and normalization.

Nonnegative eigenvalues and the implication that a nonnegative trace-zero block vanishes.
Orthonormal eigenbases of finite self-adjoint blocks.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and its leakage, weak/strong secrecy, and privacy-region definitions against the QKD page and actual item uses. This is background navigation: no classical mutual-information criterion is identified with acceptance-weighted quantum trace-distance secrecy, and no reverse implication is asserted.

The prerequisite page supplies finite quantum-information background. The QKD items invoke neither relative-entropy data processing nor strong subadditivity; their proof uses explicit classical blocks and published trace-norm results. Neither page asserts an unsupported implication between these criteria. The sum-bound argument also agrees with [Portmann–Renner, §§4.2–4.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.3525).
